(1) MARK FRESHNESS: the pre-open runs were right to flag their marks stale, and this run cleared both flags with live quotes -- the handoff pattern worked and should be repeated whenever a run fires before 09:30 ET. That is legitimately realized volatility, but it biases iv_rv_ratio LOW -- i.e. makes premium look CHEAP -- for any name that recently reported. MSFT's 0.53 and TSLA's 0.59 should NOT be read as 'cheap premium, buy single-legs' without checking whether an earnings gap is doing the work. substantive_finding.headline: FIRST post-midnight-UTC run in this automation's history -- and 'today' is dangerously ambiguous at that boundary. Three per-day artifacts would have been silently corrupted by rolling them on the UTC date. Root fix written to CLAUDE.md.
substantive_finding.how_it_surfaced: This run fired at 2026-08-14T00:45Z, i.e. 19:45 ET on THURSDAY 2026-08-13. Every prior post-close run landed before 00:00 UTC (20:28Z, 21:30Z, 22:33Z, 23:29Z), so no instance had ever faced the boundary. By UTC date, this run IS 'the first run of 2026-08-14'. By trading calendar, Friday has not begun and will not for another ~9h45m.
artifacts_at_risk: automation_heartbeat.json (dated 2026-08-13, stamped 13:05Z by that day's first run): stamping it '2026-08-14' now would PRE-SATISFY the dead-man alarm for a trading day that has not started. If the cron then died overnight, Friday would look healthy all day and the single alarm designed to catch a dead automation would never fire. This is the most dangerous of the three -- it disables a safety mechanism rather than merely producing bad data.

market_brief.json (date 2026-08-13, built 13:08Z pre-open): the run prompt says 'If market_brief.json isn't stamped today, build it.' Read on the UTC date, that instruction fires RIGHT NOW -- and a brief built at 00:45Z off overnight/thin extended-hours prints would then be stamped 2026-08-14, so Friday's genuine pre-open and first post-open runs would see it 'already stamped today' and SKIP the rebuild. Friday would be traded off Thursday-night quotes.

The -$200 realized daily loss cap and the 'max 3 new entries per day' throttle: both reset on the trading day. A UTC rollover does not hand the desk a fresh loss cap or a fresh entry budget -- and reading it that way would mean a bad Thursday could be followed by full risk appetite at 19:46 ET the same evening.
substantive_finding.action_taken: DECLINED to stamp the heartbeat, DECLINED to rebuild the brief, and treated the loss cap / entry throttle as still belonging to the 2026-08-13 session. Then made the durable fix: added a new bullet to the CLAUDE.md options-automation ruleset -- "'Today' means the US TRADING day (ET), never the UTC calendar date" -- enumerating all three artifacts and stating the rule that on any run between the 16:00 ET bell and the next 09:30 ET open, the trading day is still the day whose bell just rang. Reconcile, log, stand down; roll nothing forward. Per the standing 'fix issues at the root' principle, the next instance inherits the answer instead of re-deriving it at 00:45Z under time pressure.
substantive_finding.not_a_trading_signal: This changes no position, no size, no thesis and no risk number. It is a process defect in the run-scaffolding, caught before it cost anything.

That is a real gate doing real work, and no run this week complied-by-accident: one run noted the problem in passing ('any new entry would itself be an override requiring a written argument'), correctly, and still declined on the merits. THE_REAL_FINDING_STRUCTURAL_NOT_DRIFT.the_tension_for_RYAN_to_resolve: This looks like an unintended interaction between two rules written at different times, not a mistake by any instance. On 2026-08-05 Ryan RAISED the options budget to $1,500 precisely so the sleeve could size up on quality ('as long as the trades are quality thought out it can use up to 1500'), and authorized the hedge in the same breath. The run prompt's ~$750 soft cap on total deployed premium was written separately. Together they mean the Ryan-authorized hedge alone exhausts the soft cap, leaving the sleeve able to use only $1 of the $1,500 he approved without logging an override every time. Two coherent readings, and an agent may not pick between them: (a) the ~$750 is meant as a cap on NON-HEDGE deployed premium, in which case $751 of headroom is live and the freeze is purely opportunity-set; or (b) the ~$750 is meant as a genuine total-book ceiling, in which case the sleeve is intentionally near-frozen while the hedge is on and that should be stated so instances stop treating it as a live budget.
THE_REAL_FINDING_STRUCTURAL_NOT_DRIFT.explicitly_NOT_a_recommendation_to_loose: No unattended run may loosen a gate, and this run did not and does not propose to. Nothing here was overridden, no entry was taken, and the correct behavior in the meantime is unchanged: if a genuine A+ setup appears, write the two-sentence override argument BEFORE acting, exactly as the prompt requires. ON THE CHEAP-VOL OBJECTION: it is weaker than the prior run assumed. Within this expiry the skew RISES with strike (105C 67.90% < 115C 69.27% < 120C 70.50% IV), so a call debit spread sells a HIGHER IV than it buys -- it is not simply 'short cheap vol'. The genuine argument against the spread is different and still stands: INTC's realized vol (80%) exceeds implied (68%), meaning the stock tends to travel further than the options price, which is exactly when a capped payoff costs you most on a breakout thesis. RECOMMENDATION TO THE NEXT RUN, offered as analysis and NOT as authorization: if INTC triggers, the 2026-09-18 120C at ~$450 satisfies every constraint at once -- budget fit with room, best liquidity on the chain, right delta, long vol.

structural_finding.headline: THE AGENTIC ACCOUNT CANNOT TRADE DEBIT SPREADS. It is option_level_2; spreads require option_level_3. This is the most important thing this run produced and it is not a market observation -- it is a permanent capability limit that has been silently shaping every vehicle decision this desk has made.
structural_finding.how_it_was_found: Honestly: by accident, while trying to rescue a trade. The 16:15Z run killed AVGO -- the best candidate of the day -- on VEHICLE ECONOMICS alone, after overturning two of the four reasons the run before it had used. Its stated disqualifier was that the only earnings-clean expiry (2026-08-21, 7 DTE) bleeds ~6.8% of premium per day with a weekend to pay. The obvious repair is the desk's OWN standing preference -- 'Prefer debit spreads over single-legs at this account size' -- which nobody had actually priced today. I priced it, and then checked whether it could be executed. It cannot.
structural_finding.the_evidence: get_accounts returns option_level='option_level_2' for 718757339. The connector's own get_option_level_upgrade_info documentation states it plainly: 'option_level_2 enables long calls/puts, covered calls, and cash-secured puts; option_level_3 adds spreads and complex strategies.' Ryan's separate individual account 5ST95513 carries option_level_3 -- so the agentic account's level 2 is a per-account setting, not an account-holder limitation, which is why the approval is plausible if he applies.
structural_finding.why_it_is_dangerous_and_not_academic: This is the part a future instance must not miss. The routine prompt authorizes debit spreads 'legged ONE order at a time: long leg in first, short leg out first.' On an option_level_2 account that sequence FAILS UNSAFELY, not cleanly: the long leg FILLS, and the short leg is then REJECTED for insufficient options level. The sleeve is left holding an unintended, full-premium, naked single-leg it never decided to own -- at up to the $1,500 per-trade maximum -- with the theta profile it had specifically chosen a spread to AVOID. A run that reaches for a spread without checking the level first does not get a failed order; it gets a position. CHECK option_level BEFORE SENDING LEG ONE.
structural_finding.what_it_has_cost: Measurable, and worth stating so the upgrade case is made on numbers rather than on feel. I priced the AVGO 2026-08-28 board (14 DTE, earnings-clean, spot 394.825) live at 16:31:51Z. Single legs: 395C mid $12.85 (spread 7.78% of mid, theta -3.67%/day, but $1,285 = 86% of the per-trade max on OI 109); 410C mid $6.98 (9.31%, -6.17%/day); 420C mid $4.375 (8.00%, -8.31%/day). The corresponding VERTICALS, at mid: 395/415 debit $735, net theta -1.02%/day, BE +1.91%; 395/410 debit $587, net theta -0.70%/day, BE +1.53%; 400/420 debit $607.50, max profit $1,392.50, net theta -1.62%/day. So the structure the desk is told to prefer would have cut carry from roughly -6.8%/day to -0.7-1.6%/day -- a 4-9x improvement in exactly the variable that has now killed the day's best candidate twice -- while also HALVING the capital at risk versus the $1,285 ATM single leg. That is the cost of the missing permission, quantified.
structural_finding.what_i_did_not_do: I did not treat this discovery as a reason to trade. Finding a better vehicle does not upgrade a B setup, and 'I finally solved the structure problem, so let us use it' is precisely the momentum-toward-a-trade the mandate warns about -- the same trap the 16:15Z run flagged in itself an hour ago. AVGO fails on THESIS before it ever reaches the vehicle question (see below). The spread work is recorded as a capability finding for future setups, not as a justification for this one.

process_finding_worth_keeping.title: The iv_rv_ratio systematically lies for ~30 sessions after an earnings print, and it lies in the direction that invites bad trades.
process_finding_worth_keeping.measurement: Dropping the two largest absolute daily moves from each 30-session window: SPY 1.06->1.23, QQQ 0.89->1.10, NVDA 1.03->1.14, AMD 0.71->0.84, TSM 0.89->1.26, AVGO 1.12->1.34, MSFT 0.52->1.01, TSLA 0.72->1.24, RBRK 1.20->1.40. Six of nine flipped from 'cheap' to 'fair-to-rich'; only AMD stayed below 1.0.
process_finding_worth_keeping.why_it_matters: rv_30d is a 30-SAMPLE stdev, so one gap dominates it. Every core name printed earnings inside the current window. The desk's standing preference is to prefer IV/RV below 1.5 where history is thin -- which means the mechanical number has been quietly green-lighting premium that is not cheap.
process_finding_worth_keeping.honest_caveat: Trimming the top two moves is itself crude and UNDERSTATES fat-tail risk; a future earnings gap is a real cost the option buyer bears. Neither figure is 'the' answer. Rule adopted: log both, and pick by whether the contract expires BEFORE the next print (use ex-gap) or SPANS it (use raw).
process_finding_worth_keeping.actions: iv_history.json now carries rv_30d_ex_top2, iv_rv_ratio_ex_top2 and largest_1d_move_in_window_pct on every row. CLAUDE.md HARD RULE 8 gained a bullet stating the rule at file level.
process_finding_worth_keeping.meta_lesson: The 2026-08-13 LIN row caught this exact artifact on ONE name and nobody generalized it, so five later runs kept citing raw ratios. A lesson recorded only against a single ticker does not survive the relay -- promote it to CLAUDE.md or it dies in the file it was written in.

the_silence_decision.reasoning: The monitoring mandate's test is whether a trigger FIRES/UN-FIRES or the RECOMMENDATION changes -- not whether the number improved. The tape improving fixes the VIEW; it does not fix the VEHICLE. So 'bank it' stands.
the_silence_decision.the_asymmetry_that_settles_it: A better price can only make 'bank it' MORE right, never wrong. There is no branch on which the improved number flips his decision, so a second message buys him nothing and spends the attention the silence rule exists to protect. If he replies 'close it', he simply gets a better fill than quoted.
the_silence_decision.self_check: I tested this against the opposite reading and I want it on the record, because the pull was real. There IS a genuinely new FACT here beyond price -- the brief's confirming level re-asserted -- and that fact cuts toward the HOLD alternative, which is the one branch where new information could matter. I still judged it insufficient: theta at 21 DTE dominates a delta of -0.20, and the honest risk was that I was assembling a reason to make a quiet run feel eventful. Naming that pull is the safeguard; a run that notifies every time its book ticks favourably is how 26 messages a day get ignored and the mandate dies.

finding.verdict: CONFIRMED. The sub-hourly cron-job.org trigger has been dead for three trading days.
finding.last_sub_hourly_fire: 2026-08-18T19:46Z (14:46 CT) -- the tail of that day's configured 8:25-14:55 CT window. The job completed its normal Tuesday, then never fired again.
finding.evidence: Every run from 2026-08-19 onward lands at :18-:26 past the hour at a flat 24/day, which is exactly 24 hours x 1 -- the signature of the routine's NATIVE HOURLY backstop running alone. The 2026-08-15/16 weekend dip to 24/day is NOT part of the outage: the cron job is configured Mon-Fri, so a quiet weekend is correct behaviour and must not be read as a fourth broken day.
finding.magnitude: ~78% reduction in market-hours cadence, from ~15-minute to ~60-minute.

entries.why_the_dead_man_never_caught_it: THE IMPORTANT PART. automation_heartbeat.json is stamped by the first run of each trading day and the 20:45Z alarm fires only if NO report landed. The hourly backstop kept firing and kept stamping, so the heartbeat read healthy for three trading days while three quarters of coverage was missing. A dead-man that tests LIVENESS cannot detect DEGRADATION. Recommended durable fix, recorded in CLAUDE.md: assert a RATE, not an existence -- have the first post-open run count the prior trading day's market-hours journal entries and alarm below ~20.
entries.what_it_cost: Ryan set the per-position monitoring mandate on 2026-08-18, the same day the trigger died, so the monitoring he asked for has run at a quarter of its intended cadence ever since. Exit enforcement (-50% cuts, hard backstops) has been checking ~7x/day instead of ~31x. Binding corollary until fixed: the DTE-7 floor exists BECAUSE a 15-minute cadence cannot manage expiry-day gamma; at 60 minutes that blind spot is 4x wider, so short-DTE contracts warrant MORE caution and no run should describe the cadence as 15-minute -- it is hourly.
entries.diagnosis_handed_to_ryan: Only he can fix it; the trigger config lives on his cron-job.org account. A clean stop at a day boundary rather than a gradual fade points at, in order: (1) expired/revoked bearer token -- docs/options-automation-setup.md says '401/403 = token problem (regenerate in the routine editor, update cron-job.org)'; (2) cron-job.org auto-disabled the job after repeated failures, in which case a new token alone will NOT resume it and the job must also be re-enabled; (3) the beta header experimental-cc-routine-2026-04-01 went stale after a platform change. The execution history for the job 'Options autopilot fire' distinguishes all three by HTTP status in one look.
entries.what_this_run_did_NOT_do: Did not arm an in-session CronCreate automation to compensate. That is the retired pattern that died silently three times in one day and would put two automations on the same book. An agent can measure the cadence and report it; it cannot repair an external scheduler from inside a run, and should not imply otherwise.

finding.what: The 14:25 CT (19:25Z) EOD-report gate was calibrated for ~15-minute firing, when some run always landed inside the 14:25-15:00 CT window. With the trigger dead the routine fires hourly at :18-:26, so the last market-hours run lands at 19:21-19:24Z -- three to four minutes SHORT of the gate, every day. The gate is never satisfied pre-bell and the duty falls to a post-close run.

finding.why_nothing_errored: The report still got written every day, so no alarm fired and no run reported a failure. It was simply written late, after the market it described had closed. fix_applied.primary: Threshold moved 14:25 CT -> 14:15 CT (19:15Z), comfortably below the observed 19:21-19:24Z landing zone, so the last pre-bell run qualifies again. Committed to master, so today's ~19:2xZ run should pick it up and deliver before the bell rather than after.

fix_applied.principle_written_back: When a scheduling constant encodes an assumption about firing rate, write the fallback that does not depend on the rate. A 2-for-1 roll works: net debit ~$367, theta falls $43.96 -> $16.86/day (-62%), delta -0.344 -> -0.265, and it buys 35 extra days spanning both NVDA and the September Fed. QQQ_STRUCTURAL_ALTERNATIVES_PRICED_LIVE.D_CONVERT_TO_680_660_VERTICAL: Sell 2x the 2026-09-11 660P at the 1.86 bid = COLLECT $372. 660P mark 1.875, 1.86 x 1.89, 1.60% of mid, OI 1,856, vol 178 -- liquid enough to leg. Net basis becomes 1.945/ct = $389 capital at risk (down from $761). Theta -0.2198 + 0.1615 = -0.0583/ct = -$11.66/day for the pair, a -73% carry cut -- closely reproducing the -76% CLAUDE.md measured on this exact position on 2026-08-21. Max value 20 wide x 100 x 2 = $4,000; max profit $3,611. COST: position delta halves, -0.344 -> -0.162, and the tail below QQQ 660 is capped.
QQQ_STRUCTURAL_ALTERNATIVES_PRICED_LIVE.recommendation: IF Ryan wants to stay for the NVDA print, D is the structure that makes staying SURVIVABLE -- it converts a position that would likely decay into its own cut level before the catalyst into one that comfortably reaches it, and banks $372 doing so. IF he does not want the event exposure, A is clean at -$37 on a 1.10% spread. B -- doing nothing -- is the one option that pays full carry into a cut level and should be actively rejected rather than defaulted into. Honest counter-argument to D, stated so it is not buried: halving delta immediately before the one catalyst is the same error the routine warns against for scalps ('a spread sells away the delta and gamma you are being paid for'). D trades event upside for survival. That is the trade-off and it is Ryan's to make.

lessons_for_the_relay: THE REPORT'S RSI2 BOARD NEEDS A 'WHY IS IT DOWN' CHECK BEFORE THE CHAIN WORK, NOT AFTER. INTC's print was manufactured by a $20B secondary. The report annotates earnings on BUY lines and has no equivalent annotation for a share offering, an index deletion, a guidance cut or a downgrade -- all of which produce a clean-looking RSI2 print that is a supply event, not a mean-reversion setup. Cheapest fix available to a run today: on any RSI2 name that is down multiple sessions in a row, do the news check FIRST. It cost one web search here and killed the candidate before any thesis work.

A RISING 200-DAY MA IS NOT EVIDENCE OF AN UPTREND ON A NAME THAT HAS ROUND-TRIPPED. INTC is -36.6% off its June high and the 200d is still rising. The screen's uptrend gate passed for the wrong reason. When a report gate and the price series disagree, measure the price series.

READ THE IV PAIR BEFORE INHERITING A VEHICLE PREFERENCE. Four consecutive INTC rows handed forward 'vol is cheap, buy single legs' from raw ratios alone; the ex-gap read is 0.99, i.e. fair. A conclusion repeated across four rows is not corroboration when all four made the same measurement error.

hunt.STRUCTURAL_NOTE_worth_carrying_forward: Track A's own rule makes Friday afternoon its weakest hour, and this deserves to be stated as a pattern rather than re-derived every Friday. The mandatory time stop is 'flat by the close of the NEXT session'. A scalp opened at 14:50 ET Friday therefore has a compulsory hold spanning a full weekend gap on a 0.40-0.60 delta single leg -- the highest-gamma vehicle the desk trades, held across the one window the 15-minute cadence explicitly does not cover. That is not a reason to never scalp on a Friday, but it does mean a Friday-afternoon Track A entry needs to clear a visibly HIGHER bar than the same setup on a Tuesday, because the risk it must carry is strictly larger for the same edge. Three separate runs today have declined tactical entries partly on this ground; naming it once is cheaper than re-deriving it.
